thread:
sam: Heads-up: after last night's FlashAttention compile-flag rollout I'm seeing a p95/p99 jump on chat/generate for open-7b when seq > ~1024. p99 went from ~220ms to ~1.8s. request ids: rq_7b_abc123, rq_7b_def456.
jess: ack. which flag exactly and when was it rolled? any canary metrics?
mike: rollout history shows flag flashattn_compile=v2 pushed 2026-03-16T03:02Z across all runtime clusters. canary looked OK for short seqs.
sam: minimal repro (long prompt):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"open-7b","input":"<~1200 token prompt>","max_tokens":512}'
```
response times: 200ms -> 1.6-2.0s p99 on a couple pods.
ravi: grabbing traces now. if it's kernel selection misroute between flashattn and sdpa that could explain long-tail regressions for long seq. our selection heuristics moved to prefer flashattn for speed.
infra-bot: deploy flashattn_compile=v2 completed 2026-03-16T03:02Z; affected pools: prod-gpu-nv4-a, prod-gpu-nv4-b.
support-bot: 5 customer escalations opened, priority P1 for any paid Dedicated plans affected.
jess: can we force fallback to reference (non-flash) kernel for the model quickly? prefer quick mitigation: turn off flag or change heuristic to fall back for seq>512.
mike: quick options: 1) emergency toggle via flag rollback (fast, cluster-wide) 2) runtime rule to prefer sdpa/ref kernel for model=open-7b if seq>768 (safer) 3) patch kernel-selection code but that needs build + canary.
oncall: I'll do the emergency toggle if you want. toggling flashattn_compile to v1 will revert to previous kernels.
ravi: before toggle, we should try a narrow mitigation: push routing override for 10% traffic to fallback kernel and see p99 effect. canary gave false confidence because we tested mostly short prompts.
sam: agree. open-7b long-seq traffic is only ~3% of requests but drives p99 for some customers. fallback 10% then 50% then full if stable.
jess: add repro steps to the incident ticket: provide request ids, pod ids: pod-prod-23a, pod-prod-23b, logs: 
```
[2026-03-16T03:10:22Z] rq_7b_abc123 kernel=flashattn compile_flag=v2 latency=1842ms seq_len=1248 pod=pod-prod-23a
[2026-03-16T03:10:24Z] rq_7b_def456 kernel=flashattn compile_flag=v2 latency=1970ms seq_len=1302 pod=pod-prod-23b
```
mike: traced to kernel hotpath: kernel-launch times spike when sequence crosses 1024 boundary. SDPA fallback path doesn't spike. suspect memory layout or attention tiling.
ravi: I'm spinning a debug build with extra kernel logging to repro locally on devbox. ETA 45m.
oncall: toggling plan: 1) route 10% to fallback kernel via runtime rule now, 2) monitor p95/p99 for 15m, 3) if improves, widen to 50% then 100% or do full rollback.
sam: I'm in favor of the runtime rule first. please also add a short-term alert to suppress noisy SLO alerts for the rollout so we don't drown.
jess: created incident INC-20260316-47 with notes and customers, linking thread.
mike: PR in progress to add a hysteresis check to kernel selector: only pick flashattn if avg seq < 700 and p99 delta < 200ms. will post PR link when ready.
ravi: debug build repro shows that FlashAttention kernel uses a tiling path that hits an O(N^2) memcpy for certain pad sizes. reproduces on local with model weights+seq=1200.
sam: good find. that explains long-tail. ok plan: implement runtime rule fallback + suppress alerts + prepare rollback if rule doesn't help.
oncall: executing step 1 now: applying routing override for model=open-7b -> kernel=ref-kernel for 10% traffic.
infra-bot: routing rule applied: rule-id rr-20260316-09; 10% of open-7b traffic routed to ref-kernel.
support-bot: update: two customers reported lower latency after rule applied.
jess: monitor telemetry for 20m and decide. mike/ravi, can you prioritize the kernel fix and a unit test to catch the memcpy edge case?
mike: will add unit + integration test that exercises seq sizes around tiling boundaries (e.g., 1008, 1024, 1200) and run on CI quantized build.
ravi: debug build patch ready, uploading to canary now.
sam: once canary passes (p99 back to baseline), let's roll to 50% then full and then plan a proper revert/patch release for tomorrow.
jess: thanks all. I'll update the incident and customer comms. please drop any additional logs or repros here. :thumbsup:
